fha.fcDesc: Erroneous channel-A surface response to command
fha.effAc: One channel of the dual fly-by-wire flight control commands a surface response different from that intended; aircraft-level trajectory effect depends on whether channel B cross-compare detects the disagreement and transfers control, and on mechanical reversion availability — not determinable from the SF-001 function definition alone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SF-001 is a single-channel function; its aircraft effect cannot be derived without asserting channel-B transfer/mechanical-reversion behaviour, which is an architecture claim outside this function's definition. Belongs in SFHA (FCA scope) up-linked to the aircraft 'Control aircraft trajectory' condition. No aircraft effect stated ⇒ cannot classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded channel-A surface motion
fha.effAc: Channel A drives a surface half without a corresponding pilot/autopilot command; aircraft-level trajectory effect depends on cross-compare detection, channel-B transfer and mechanical reversion — not determinable from the SF-001 function definition alone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — New condition not in current FCIM; single-channel scope. Aircraft effect requires an untasked channel-B/reversion independence claim to state, so it cannot be derived here. No aircraft effect stated ⇒ cannot classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous channel-A surface command
fha.effAc: Channel A issues an erroneous surface command that the monitored cross-compare fails to flag; without detection there is no automatic transfer to channel B, so the erroneous command persists. Aircraft-level trajectory consequence still depends on the surviving channel/reversion architecture and cannot be quantified from the SF-001 function definition alone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Single-channel, crew-unaware condition; the aircraft effect turns on whether an undetected erroneous command can propagate through the dual-channel monitor — an independence/monitor-coverage claim not established by the SF-001 definition. No aircraft effect stated ⇒ cannot classify. Belongs in SFHA (FCA) with an AFHA up-link.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected channel-A surface drift
fha.effAc: Channel A surface position drifts slowly from commanded without triggering the cross-compare threshold; aircraft-level trajectory effect depends on monitor coverage of slow drift and on channel-B/reversion availability — not determinable from the SF-001 function definition alone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — New condition not in current FCIM; single-channel, crew-unaware. Aircraft effect requires a monitor-coverage and independence claim to state and cannot be derived from the function definition. No aircraft effect stated ⇒ cannot classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of channel-A flight control
fha.effAc: Reduced flight control authority through channel A's half of each surface pair; the surfaces are sized so one half of each pair is sufficient and channel B remains, so aircraft-level trajectory effect depends on that surviving-half sizing and channel-B availability — not derivable from the SF-001 function definition alone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Single-channel partial loss; stating the aircraft effect requires the sizing/redundancy claim (one surface half sufficient, channel B available), which is an architecture claim outside SF-001's definition. No aircraft effect stated ⇒ cannot classify. Belongs in SFHA (FCA) up-linked to the aircraft 'Control aircraft trajectory' condition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of channel-A flight control — outside maximum authorised configuration (MAC)
fha.effAc: Channel A no longer commands its half of each surface pair. Per SDD §5.6.3 each channel alone is sufficient and transfer to channel B is automatic and annunciated; the aircraft continues to be controlled on channel B, with mechanical reversion remaining below both channels. Loss of one of two independent control channels is a reduction in available control redundancy. 'Outside MAC' condition and its distinguishing effect are not defined by the provided function definition.
fha.effCrew: Channel transfer is annunciated (SDD §5.6.6). Crew monitor degraded-redundancy state; degraded laws are annunciated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition (SF-001 'Provide primary flight control via channel A') and SDD establish that single-channel loss is covered by channel B plus mechanical reversion, which alone would support Major (significant reduction in redundancy). However the 'outside MAC' qualifier that distinguishes this condition (versus the within-MAC loss) is not defined in the provided inputs — its aircraft effect cannot be stated, so severity cannot be derived without guessing. Awaiting the MAC definition / configuration boundary.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous channel-B surface response to command
fha.effAc: Channel B drives its half of each surface pair erroneously relative to the issued command. Per SDD §5.7.2/§5.7.3 the monitored cross-compare of surface position between channels detects the disagreement and automatic transfer to channel A follows; the aircraft is controlled on channel A with mechanical reversion below. A detected erroneous single-channel command produces a transient before the annunciated transfer arrests it, a significant reduction in safety margin during the transient but not loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Disagreement is annunciated; transfer is automatic (SDD §5.7.3). Crew manage a degraded-redundancy configuration; degraded laws annunciated.
fha.effPax: Possible transient motion during the pre-transfer excursion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects derived above: the monitored cross-compare detects the erroneous channel-B command and automatic annunciated transfer to channel A caps the excursion; result is a significant reduction in control-redundancy / safety margin with a controllable transient, matching a significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities. Assumes the cross-compare detects this erroneous-response mode within a benign transient — an independence/coverage assumption logged as Open. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded channel-B surface motion
fha.effAc: Channel B produces surface motion absent a command. Per SDD §5.7.3 the monitored cross-compare of surface position detects the disagreement and automatic annunciated transfer to channel A follows; control continues on channel A with mechanical reversion below. Detected uncommanded single-channel motion produces a transient excursion arrested by the transfer — a significant reduction in safety margin during the transient, not loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Disagreement and transfer annunciated (SDD §5.7.3). Crew manage degraded redundancy.
fha.effPax: Possible transient motion during the pre-transfer excursion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: monitored cross-compare detects the uncommanded motion and automatic annunciated transfer to channel A bounds the excursion; significant reduction in safety margin with a controllable transient. Same detection-coverage/independence assumption as SF-002-M, logged Open. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous channel-B surface command
fha.effAc: Channel B issues an erroneous surface command that is NOT detected by the cross-compare monitor. With the monitored transfer defeated (crew unaware, no annunciation, no transfer to channel A), the erroneous command persists and drives an uncorrected surface excursion. An unbounded erroneous command on one half of the surface pairs, without the automatic transfer that otherwise arrests it, is a large reduction in safety margins and functional capability and could progress toward loss of control depending on authority and phase.
fha.effCrew: By definition unaware: no annunciation, crew continue duties and take no action regarding it; workload rises sharply only once the resulting flight-path departure becomes apparent.
fha.effPax: Excursion / abnormal attitude potentially causing distress or injury.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from the undetected/unaware effects above: defeating the cross-compare removes the automatic annunciated transfer that bounds the detected cases (M/M2), so the erroneous single-channel command persists uncorrected — a large reduction in safety margins/functional capability, matching Hazardous. Whether it reaches Catastrophic depends on the channel-B surface authority envelope and worst-phase timing, which the provided function definition does not quantify; flagged. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected channel-B surface drift
fha.effAc: Channel B allows a slow, undetected drift of its half of the surface pairs away from the commanded position, below the cross-compare detection threshold. With the monitored transfer not triggered (crew unaware), a progressive control error accumulates; the aircraft-level consequence — from a manageable trim/asymmetry offset to a significant safety-margin reduction — depends on the drift rate and the monitor's detection threshold, neither of which is defined in the provided function definition.
fha.effCrew: By definition unaware: no annunciation; crew continue duties normally until the accumulated error produces a discernible flight-path or trim cue.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Undetected surface drift' is not defined in the provided inputs, and the SDD does not state the cross-compare detection threshold or the channel-B surface drift authority. The aircraft effect scales between a benign trim offset and a significant margin reduction depending entirely on those undefined parameters, so severity cannot be derived without guessing. Awaiting the cross-compare detection threshold and channel-B surface-authority envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of channel-B flight control (channel B degraded, channel A available)
fha.effAc: Channel B drives one half of each surface pair; on a monitored disagreement transfer to channel A is automatic and annunciated. Aircraft remains controllable through channel A, which alone is sufficient as each surface pair is sized so one half is adequate.
fha.effCrew: Degraded-law/transfer annunciated; crew continues on the operative channel with slight increase in monitoring.
fha.effPax: No effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Automatic annunciated transfer to a sufficient channel A leaves a slight reduction in safety margins and slight crew workload increase. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of channel-B flight control — outside MAC
fha.effAc: Channel A remains available and alone sufficient to fly the aircraft; the 'outside MAC' qualifier is not defined in the SDD against a single-channel capability, so a distinct aircraft effect cannot be grounded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect for the 'outside MAC' qualifier: the SDD states channel A alone is sufficient but does not define the MAC boundary or any single-channel envelope restriction that would distinguish this condition. Missing: definition of 'outside MAC' and the residual capability/envelope with only channel A operating.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of mechanical control reversion
fha.effAc: Mechanical reversion covers pitch trim and the lower rudder segment only and is not a selectable mode — it is what remains when both channels are gone. A partial loss manifests as an aircraft effect only in combination with loss of both fly-by-wire channels; the SDD does not characterise the residual manual capability, so an aircraft-level effect cannot be grounded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reversion is a residual path active only after dual-channel loss; the SDD does not state the aircraft effect of a partial reversion loss on its own. Missing: the combined failure state and the residual controllability afforded by partial mechanical reversion.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of mechanical control reversion
fha.effAc: The mechanical path is the last-resort control that remains after loss of both flight control channels; its complete loss removes that final reversion. An aircraft-level effect arises only combined with dual-channel loss, a combined state the SDD does not characterise, so severity cannot be grounded standalone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The reversion path has no aircraft effect until both channels are lost; classifying its standalone loss would require the combined-failure state the SDD does not provide. Missing: the dual-channel-loss context and the resulting controllability with vs without mechanical reversion.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous left thrust response to command
fha.effAc: Erroneous left thrust (e.g. thrust different from commanded) could induce asymmetry; the two thrust levers are mechanically independent and not ganged, and feather is available. The aircraft effect depends on the magnitude and sign of the thrust error and on crew detection/response, none of which the SDD quantifies, so an aircraft effect cannot be grounded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect: the SDD does not state the magnitude range of an erroneous thrust response, the resulting yaw/asymmetry, or the crew detection means and reversion for this malfunction. Missing: erroneous-thrust magnitude bounds, asymmetry consequence, and detection/mitigation (feather/annunciation) coverage.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded left propulsion thrust change
fha.effAc: An uncommanded change in left thrust produces a thrust asymmetry against the right unit, yawing/rolling the aircraft; at low speed/low altitude (take-off, initial climb, water run) the asymmetry must be arrested by the crew and offending unit managed to retain controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect yaw/roll and thrust cues, apply directional control and manage the affected side (retard lever, feather); increased workload in a critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (asymmetric thrust, controllability/workload at low speed) but the magnitude of the uncommanded change (transient vs sustained, full-scale vs partial) is not stated by the function definition, so whether the outcome is a large or significant reduction in safety margins is not determined from the inputs; cannot classify without the excursion magnitude and controllability outcome.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous left propulsion thrust command
fha.effAc: An erroneous left-thrust command that is not annunciated produces a thrust asymmetry the crew are not alerted to; the aircraft yaws/rolls and departs the intended trajectory before the crew diagnose the source, with the largest margin loss at low speed and low altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action regarding the erroneous command until they detect the resulting flight-path/attitude deviation, delaying recovery and compounding the excursion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected/erroneous asymmetric thrust with delayed crew action tends toward a more severe class than the aware case, but the function definition does not state the commanded error magnitude or the resulting controllability outcome, so the reduction-in-safety-margins band cannot be derived from the inputs; classification withheld pending the erroneous-command magnitude and recovery outcome.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of left propulsion thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced thrust from the left unit against full right thrust produces a thrust asymmetry and a reduction in total available thrust; the sizing case is continuation of a coastal sector on the remaining capability, with the affected propeller feathered if the reduction is toward loss so the pair-level rating holds.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage the affected side (derate annunciation, lever, feather-on-lock), trim the asymmetry and continue or divert; increased workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD grounds continued flight on the remaining unit and derate/feather management, but the degree of partial loss and its asymmetry effect on controllability and climb margin at low speed are not fixed by the function definition, so the reduction-in-safety-margins band is not derivable from the inputs; classification withheld pending the degraded-thrust level and its performance/controllability effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of left propulsion thrust
fha.effAc: Complete loss of the left unit leaves the aircraft on the right unit alone; the pair is sized for one-unit continuation of a coastal sector, with the failed-side windmilling propeller feathered so the remaining unit's rating is sufficient. Reduced total thrust and an initial yaw/roll asymmetry until trimmed.
fha.effCrew: Crew feather the failed side (automatic on locked rotor, or the guarded switch), trim the asymmetry, and continue or divert on the remaining unit; increased workload, particularly if the loss occurs at low speed after take-off.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD supports continued flight on one unit once feathered, which bounds the away-from-benign end, but whether an engine-out at the most critical low-speed/low-altitude point remains within controllability and climb margins is not determined by the function definition alone; the reduction-in-safety-margins band therefore cannot be derived from the inputs. Classification withheld pending one-unit take-off/climb performance and V-speed substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous right propulsion thrust response to command
fha.effAc: The right unit produces thrust different from that commanded, creating a thrust asymmetry against the left unit and a departure from the intended trajectory; crew are annunciated/aware and act to arrest the asymmetry and manage the affected side.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the mismatch (thrust cues, powertrain page, yaw/roll), apply directional control and manage the right side (retard lever, feather); increased workload in critical phases.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (erroneous right thrust, asymmetry, crew management) but the magnitude of the erroneous response and the resulting controllability outcome are not stated by the function definition, so the reduction-in-safety-margins band cannot be derived from the inputs; classification withheld pending the error magnitude and controllability/workload outcome.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded propeller feather — asymmetric (single side feathers without command)
fha.effAc: Sudden loss of one propulsion unit's thrust contribution and a resulting thrust/yaw asymmetry; the remaining unit is sized to continue a sector alone but with reduced margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the asymmetry, apply directional control and manage the reversion; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent single-side feather yields a thrust asymmetry and a large reduction in handling/safety margins, particularly at take-off/climb, without loss of the aircraft. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propeller feather (feather unavailable on demand)
fha.effAc: On loss of a propulsion unit the failed propeller cannot be feathered; the windmilling drag degrades the one-engine-inoperative case, for which the single-unit rating assumes feathering of the failed side.
fha.effCrew: Crew manages a degraded OEI condition with reduced climb/continuation capability; increased workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of feather undermines the sizing case for continuing on one unit, giving a large reduction in safety margins/functional capability without necessarily losing the aircraft. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of propeller feather (feather latently unavailable, crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Feather is latently unavailable; on a subsequent propulsion-unit failure the failed propeller windmills undetected until demanded, degrading the OEI case the single-unit rating depends on.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action on the latent condition; the degraded OEI capability is only discovered when feather is demanded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent loss of feather, discovered only when a propulsion unit fails, produces the same degraded OEI margin without prior warning — a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary flight indication (misleading attitude/air-data on the primary display)
fha.effAc: Misleading primary attitude/air-data is presented; an independent standby display and flight-control channel B read a separate source and the primary-vs-standby cross-compare disagreement is annunciated, so an independent reference remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the annunciated cross-compare disagreement and revert to the standby reference; increased workload and potential for control error if the disagreement is not resolved.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading primary flight information can lead to a large reduction in safety margins if acted upon; mitigated but not eliminated by the annunciated cross-compare and the independent standby source. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous powertrain indication (misleading SOC / available-power / loop-temperature on the powertrain page)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition establishes that misleading powertrain state (SOC, available power, loop temperature) mis-informs energy-management decisions on a hybrid aircraft, but the provided inputs do not establish an aircraft-level effect (e.g. whether an independent cross-check of powertrain state exists, or the outcome of acting on the erroneous data) sufficient to derive a severity; needs the powertrain-state cross-check architecture and the operational consequence of a mis-managed reserve.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous primary flight indication (attitude / air data) presented to the crew, primary and standby sources not annunciating a disagreement
fha.effAc: Crew fly to erroneous attitude/air-data with no alert; FCA reads the same primary sensor set (§5.10) so control-law inputs may be corrupted concurrently; potential departure from intended flightpath and loss of control, most critical in IMC in the low flight levels where the aircraft operates.
fha.effCrew: No cross-compare alert to prompt reference to the standby source; crew act on false information believing it valid.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to loss-of-control outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected erroneous attitude/air data acted upon in IMC can drive an unrecoverable departure; SDD notes primary/standby disagreement is annunciated rather than voted (§5.10.3), so the UNAWARE case removes the mitigation that would otherwise apply. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous powertrain indication (state of charge / available power / loop temperature) presented to the crew
fha.effCrew: Crew make energy-management and diversion decisions on false powertrain state on a hybrid aircraft where 'how much flying is left' is not answered by a fuel gauge (§5.10.2).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect cannot be grounded from the function definition alone: whether erroneous SOC/available-power indication leads to premature energy exhaustion or an unnecessary/late diversion depends on energy-reserve sizing and crew procedure, which the SDD flags as preliminary and does not classify. Needs the powertrain reserve case and crew energy-management procedure to derive an aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight display (e.g. loss of one display unit) with the primary flight picture still available on the remaining unit
fha.effAc: Full flight picture retained on the remaining primary unit (§5.10.3); no loss of attitude/air data to either pilot; flightpath control unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Reduced display resource, slight increase in monitoring workload; degradation annunciated.
fha.effPax: No effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one display unit leaves the other presenting the full picture (§5.10.3); effect is a slight increase in crew workload with no reduction in flightpath control. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of powertrain indication (loss of one or more powertrain parameters — SOC, available power or loop temperature — with the flight picture retained)
fha.effCrew: Reduced insight into energy state and thermal derate margin; crew energy-management and derate awareness degraded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect not determinable from the function definition: consequence of losing a powertrain parameter depends on which parameter, remaining indication, and the energy-reserve/derate procedure. The SDD describes the powertrain page but does not establish reserve margins or crew reliance, so the effect on safety margins cannot be stated without guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight and powertrain display (both primary display units / primary sensor set lost)
fha.effAc: Crew reverts to the standby display, which presents attitude and air data on an entirely separate source, probe, electrical channel and battery (§5.11); FCB reads the standby source so flightpath control remains available. Powertrain indication (SOC / available power / loop temperature) is lost with no standby equivalent. Reduced information margin, most demanding in IMC.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload flying on the standby instrument alone; loss of consolidated crew alerting hosted in the primary display (§5.10.2) and loss of powertrain/energy state.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to increased crew workload; controlled flight retained.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the full primary picture and the consolidated crew-alerting function, leaving a single standby attitude/air-data source and no powertrain indication, is a large reduction in functional capability and a significant increase in crew workload; controlled flight is retained via standby + FCB (§5.11), so effects support Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. Engineer to confirm against the standby-only handling case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby attitude indication (crew aware via primary/standby cross-compare)
fha.effAc: Standby attitude source disagrees with the primary picture; the continuous primary-vs-standby cross-compare annunciates a disagreement (SDD §5.10.3). No automatic resolution — the design does not vote two sources. Flight control channel B, which reads the standby set, may act on corrupted attitude until the crew de-selects to the primary/channel-A picture.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by annunciated cross-compare disagreement; must identify the valid source and revert to the primary display and channel A. Increased workload to diagnose and reconfigure.
fha.effPax: No direct effect while the crew retain a valid primary attitude reference and revert.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the disagreement annunciated and a valid primary source and channel A available, the effect is a significant increase in crew workload to identify and reject the erroneous source; effects do not reach a large reduction in safety margin because a trustworthy independent reference remains. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby air-data indication (crew aware via primary/standby cross-compare)
fha.effAc: Standby air-data (from the second probe) disagrees with the primary air-data set; the primary-vs-standby cross-compare annunciates a disagreement (SDD §5.10.3, §5.11). Flight control channel B reads the standby air data and may command on corrupted airspeed/altitude until the crew revert to the primary source and channel A.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by annunciated disagreement; must determine the valid air-data source and revert. Increased workload; potential for transient mis-flown speed/altitude before reversion.
fha.effPax: No direct effect while the crew retain and revert to a valid primary air-data reference.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Annunciated disagreement with a valid primary air-data source and channel A available limits the effect to a significant workload increase to reject the erroneous source; a trustworthy independent air-data reference remains, so the effect does not reach a large reduction in safety margin. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous standby attitude indication (crew unaware; cross-compare not effective, crew continue duties)
fha.effAc: Standby attitude is erroneous but the disagreement is not detected/annunciated or is disregarded; the crew take no corrective action. Flight control channel B acts on corrupted attitude, and should a subsequent loss shift command reliance to the standby-fed channel, the aircraft may be flown on misleading attitude with no trustworthy independent reference to expose the error — potential loss of control, most critical at low altitude and in IMC.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the error and continue normal duties; misleading attitude may drive an inappropriate control response, particularly in instrument conditions where no outside horizon corroborates.
fha.effPax: Exposed to the consequences of a potential loss of aircraft control if the error is acted upon without an independent cross-check.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the class from the aircraft-level function alone: the SDD does not state whether an undetected standby-attitude error can propagate to an actual loss of control given channel-A independence and the primary display remaining valid (SDD §5.11.3). Whether the outcome is Hazardous (misleading data on one redundant channel) or Catastrophic (loss of control if the standby-fed path becomes the acting reference) needs the crew-detection window and the channel-B command authority under a concurrent primary/channel-A failure — engineering judgement / PSSA input, not stated here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous standby air-data indication (crew unaware; cross-compare not effective, crew continue duties)
fha.effAc: Standby air-data is erroneous but undetected; the crew take no corrective action. Flight control channel B acts on corrupted airspeed/altitude, and if command reliance shifts to the standby-fed channel the aircraft may be flown to misleading speed/altitude with no trustworthy independent reference to expose the error — risk of speed/altitude excursion outside the safe envelope, most critical during take-off, approach and landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue normal duties; misleading air data may drive an inappropriate speed/altitude response with no corroborating source flagged.
fha.effPax: Exposed to the consequences of a speed/altitude excursion if the erroneous air data is acted upon without an independent cross-check.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the class from the aircraft-level function alone: the SDD does not state whether an undetected standby air-data error can propagate to a hazardous/catastrophic excursion given channel-A independence and the primary set remaining valid. Whether Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on the crew-detection window and channel-B command authority under a concurrent primary/channel-A air-data failure — engineering judgement / PSSA input, not stated here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of standby attitude indication
fha.effAc: Standby attitude indication is degraded (reduced capability or intermittent) but not wholly lost. The primary display and its independent sensor set remain the working reference, and flight control channel A remains available; the standby set is the backup/redundancy layer (SDD §5.11.3), so degradation reduces the depth of independent backup available to channel B without removing the primary picture.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain the full primary attitude picture; awareness of degraded standby capability and monitoring of the primary source. Slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: No direct effect while the primary attitude reference remains fully available.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one layer of the independent standby/backup with the primary attitude reference and channel A intact is a significant reduction in remaining functional capability/redundancy depth rather than a slight one, given the standby set is the dissimilar backup and a channel-B sensor source; effects do not reach a large reduction in safety margin because the primary picture is unaffected. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of standby attitude and air-data indication — reduced standby air-data capability with primary set available
fha.effAc: Reduced independent air-data source; the standby display also feeds flight control channel B, so a partial loss of standby air data degrades channel B's sensing while the primary set and channel A remain available. Cross-compare between primary and standby continues.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain the primary picture; standby annunciates degradation. Increased monitoring and cross-check workload.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects support a significant reduction in redundancy of the independent standby source and a degradation to one dissimilar flight-control channel, with primary indication and channel A intact — a significant reduction in functional capability / safety margin, not a large one. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of standby attitude and air-data indication
fha.effAc: Loss of the sole independent standby attitude/air-data source. Because channel B reads the standby set, its loss removes both the independent crew reversion picture and channel B's sensing source; the aircraft is left on the primary sensor set and channel A, removing the dissimilar-source protection against a primary air-data fault.
fha.effCrew: Loss of the independent standby reference; crew reliant on the primary picture with no dissimilar cross-check. Increased workload and reduced ability to detect a misleading primary source.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The stated effect is a large reduction in functional capability and safety margin — loss of the aircraft's only dissimilar/independent air-data reference plus degradation of one flight-control channel's source, removing the design's protection against a common air-data fault. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent landing gear retraction
fha.effAc: Uncommanded retraction with the aircraft on a paved surface collapses the gear and results in structural contact with the runway; on a water approach with gear correctly stowed the condition is not applicable. Retraction interlock also retracts the water rudder.
fha.effCrew: Sudden loss of the correct landing configuration; limited time to react during take-off/landing.
fha.effPax: Potential for injury from a gear-collapse ground contact.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects on the ground/landing phase support a large reduction in safety margin with potential serious injury; whether an in-flight uncommanded retraction is credible (versus weight-on-wheels inhibited) is an architectural question the SDD does not fully resolve. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position indication — crew aware
fha.effAc: One sensor set reports erroneously, but the design presents a comparison of two dissimilar sensors against the selected landing surface and annunciates a mismatch; the aircraft configuration itself is unaffected and the crew are alerted to the disagreement.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive a mismatch annunciation and apply the mismatch procedure, cross-checking against the selected surface. Increased workload during the approach.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the mismatch annunciated and dissimilar comparison available, the effect is a significant increase in crew workload during approach with the true configuration recoverable — a significant, not large, reduction. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous gear position indication — crew unaware
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar sensor means agree on an incorrect position with no mismatch annunciation; on an amphibian the same configuration that is correct for a runway is wrong for water, so an undetected wrong indication can lead the crew to land in the wrong configuration for the surface (gear down on water, or gear up on land).
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally, unaware; they act on a wrong-but-agreeing indication and may commit to an incorrect landing configuration.
fha.effPax: Potential for injury from an incorrect-configuration landing (gear-down water landing or gear-up runway landing).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The unaware effect — an undetected wrong configuration for the landing surface with potential serious injury — supports a large reduction in safety margin; classification could reach Catastrophic depending on the outcome of an incorrect water/runway configuration landing, which requires the SFHA/occupant-outcome analysis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of landing gear extension — asymmetric (one or more units fail to reach a locked-down position while others extend)
fha.effAc: Aircraft presents an asymmetric/incomplete gear configuration for a land landing; touchdown on an unlocked or retracted unit degrades ground handling and risks structural damage on the paved-runway landing. Water landings are on the hull and unaffected by gear position.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by the position comparison against selected landing surface; assumed to reconfigure, attempt mechanical free-fall extension, and if unsuccessful elect an alternate surface (water) — a significant increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a harder or abnormal land touchdown if a locked configuration cannot be achieved.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in functional capability (one landing surface degraded) with a significant increase in crew workload; mechanical free-fall extension and reversion to a water landing remain available, so effects fall short of Hazardous. Confirm against the free-fall independence claim. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of gear position indication (one sensor set or one channel's indication lost; comparison degraded)
fha.effAc: Each lock is sensed by two dissimilar, independent means and power is split across both channels, so a partial loss degrades the comparison presented to the crew rather than the gear's ability to extend; the mismatch alerting against selected landing surface may be reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains at least one position source per affected unit and the surface-mismatch alert; the effect on crew ability to confirm a safe configuration depends on whether a usable comparison survives, which is not established at aircraft level here.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD supports the architecture (two dissimilar sensors per lock, dual-channel power) but does not define the aircraft-level outcome of a partial indication loss — specifically whether the crew is left with an ambiguous or a still-usable configuration confirmation. Without that, the effect cannot be driven to a class; needs engineering judgement on the degraded-comparison case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of landing gear extension (no unit reaches a locked-down position by normal or emergency means)
fha.effAc: No usable gear configuration for a paved-runway landing; the aircraft must divert to a water landing on the hull, which is a designed capability of the amphibian. A forced gear-up land landing would risk substantial structural damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted, attempt normal then mechanical free-fall extension, and on failure elect a water landing within the declared sea state — a significant increase in workload and a constrained diversion set.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a water landing (a normal operating surface for this aircraft) or, if no water is reachable, a gear-up land landing.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On this amphibian a water landing is a designed operating surface, so complete loss of gear extension removes one landing-surface option rather than the ability to land — a significant reduction in capability with increased workload. If water is not always reachable at the diversion point the effect could rise; confirm against the operating concept before committing. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded water-rudder deflection (water rudder deflects other than as commanded during water operation)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded deflection of the deployed water rudder produces an unintended yaw/heading on the water; directional control on the water can be recovered by the manual release (retracting the blade) with reversion to differential thrust.
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives heading deviation and yaw cues on the water, retracts the blade via the manual release and steers on differential thrust — an increase in workload during a low-speed water phase.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a transient heading excursion during water taxi/take-off.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Occurs at low speed on the water where recovery (manual retraction, differential thrust) is available and the air rudder is unaffected; slight reduction in safety margin with a slight workload increase. Confirm the water-take-off speed regime does not elevate this. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent water-rudder deployment (blade extends when it should be retracted)
fha.effAc: A deployed water rudder at the sternpost during take-off, landing or land operations is out of its intended envelope; the hardwired gear-down interlock is designed to retract the blade on selecting gear down for a land landing, which mitigates the land case.
fha.effCrew: Position is annunciated; crew commanded to retract and, if the interlock has not, uses the manual release — an increase in workload at a high-workload phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level effect of a deployed water rudder during high-speed take-off/landing (drag, structural load on the blade, directional effect) is not characterised in the SDD, and the residual case where the hardwired retraction interlock does not act is not defined at aircraft level. Cannot derive a class without that effect; needs engineering judgement on the deployed-blade loads and the interlock-failure residual.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous water-rudder position indication — crew unaware, water rudder position mis-indicated
fha.effAc: Water-rudder position shown to crew does not match true blade position; the interlock is hardwired to gear selection (§5.13.2) so retraction on gear-down is unaffected, but a mis-indicated deployed/retracted state can lead to an unexpected water-handling response during taxi and the take-off water run. Airborne flight path is unaffected — the water rudder is retracted for take-off, landing and all land operations.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on erroneous position indication; directional response on the water differs from expectation, increasing workload during a low-speed water manoeuvre.
fha.effPax: No direct effect during a water manoeuvre.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are confined to water taxi/low-speed water manoeuvring; directional control reverts to differential thrust (§5.13.3) and the gear interlock is hardwired, so the mis-indication produces a slight increase in crew workload without a reduction in flight safety margins. Confirm the water-run exposure does not warrant Major. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of water directional control — reduced water-rudder authority
fha.effAc: Reduced directional authority on the water; the aircraft is harder to hold on heading during water taxi and the take-off water run within the declared sea state. Directional control on the water is still available via differential thrust.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain water heading using thrust and reduced rudder authority.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced water directional authority is a slight reduction of a water-manoeuvring margin recoverable by differential thrust (§5.13.3); no airborne or land effect. Confirm the take-off water-run case does not push this to Major given crosswind/sea-state. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of water directional control — water rudder inoperative
fha.effAc: Water rudder inoperative; the sole remaining means of directional control on the water is differential thrust (§5.13.3). Heading holding during water taxi and the take-off/landing water run is degraded, with the failed blade recoverable to a retracted position by a manual release in the aft cabin. No airborne or land-operation effect — the water rudder is retracted for those phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew maintain water heading on differential thrust alone and may execute the manual retraction release; significant increase in workload during a confined-water manoeuvre.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the primary water directional-control means is a significant reduction of a water-manoeuvring capability with reversion available (differential thrust, manual retraction); it produces a significant increase in crew workload during water operations without an airborne safety-margin reduction. Confirm the worst-case confined-water/sea-state exposure does not exceed Major. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fire or thermal warning — false fire/overheat indication to the crew
fha.effAc: A false fire/overheat warning may prompt crew-commanded isolation responses — fuel shutoff to the turbogenerator, propulsion-bus contactor open and feather (§5.15.4) — resulting in unnecessary loss of an energy source or a propulsion unit if the crew act on the false alert. Dual-loop AND arrangement (§5.15.2) makes a single-loop-induced false warning less likely.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to a false warning; a diversion or unnecessary isolation/feather increases workload and may reduce available propulsion or energy margin needlessly.
fha.effPax: Possible unnecessary diversion or reduced comfort; no direct injury from the erroneous warning itself.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false warning that leads the crew to isolate an energy source or feather a propulsion unit produces a significant increase in crew workload and a possible unnecessary reduction of propulsion/energy capability on a twin arrangement, without in itself endangering the flight given the remaining source. Confirm the worst credible crew response (loss of one energy source in the take-off/climb band) does not warrant Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected fire or thermal condition — real fire/overheat not annunciated, crew unaware
fha.effAc: A genuine fire, overheat or energy-store thermal-runaway condition progresses without warning; the crew take no isolation, containment-monitoring or feather action because they are unaware. In the store bay, containment and the overboard vent are designed to hold a single-module event (§5.15.2), but without the thermal-event annunciation the crew cannot initiate isolation or the associated procedure; in the generator or nacelle zones an undetected fire may propagate before isolation/suppression is commanded.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no fire response; first indication is uncontained damage or a secondary effect, by which point the condition may be advanced.
fha.effPax: Potential exposure to fire, smoke or thermal-runaway products if the condition propagates to an occupied compartment before being noticed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected fire/thermal condition removes the crew's opportunity to isolate, contain or suppress, allowing propagation toward a large reduction in safety margins; the store enclosure provides passive containment for a single-module event but generator/nacelle propagation without detection can be more severe. Confirm whether the store-bay containment credit and a credible worst-case propagation warrant Catastrophic rather than Hazardous. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and thermal detection — detection lost in one or more, but not all, of the four monitored zones (store bay, turbogenerator, two nacelles) or cabin/baggage.
fha.effAc: Fire, overheat or thermal-runaway onset in an affected zone is not annunciated; containment (store bay), isolation (nacelles) and extinguishant (generator bay) responses are not triggered in that zone, allowing an event to develop undetected in that zone while other zones remain covered.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no warning for the affected zone and take no timely isolation or procedural action there; other zones still annunciate.
fha.effPax: Potential exposure to an undetected fire/thermal event developing in the affected zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of detection in a fire zone removes the trigger for the designed containment/isolation/extinguishant response there, permitting an undetected event to develop — a large reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities; classified Hazardous pending confirmation of which zones and the residual protection. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and thermal detection — no fire, overheat or thermal-runaway sensing in any monitored zone or the cabin/baggage.
fha.effAc: No annunciation of fire, overheat or thermal runaway anywhere on the aircraft; none of the automatic responses that depend on detection (store-bay containment awareness, generator-bay extinguishant discharge, nacelle isolation/feather, fuel shutoff, bus contactor-open) are triggered, so any fire/thermal event develops undetected across a hybrid powertrain with a high-voltage store.
fha.effCrew: Crew have no warning of any fire or thermal event and take no isolation, discharge or procedural action; the crew-alerting fire prioritisation is unavailable.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to an undetected in-flight fire or thermal-runaway event with no crew response.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected in-flight fire or thermal-runaway event on an aircraft carrying a high-voltage energy store, with no crew warning and no triggered containment/isolation/suppression, can progress to loss of the aircraft; classified Catastrophic pending confirmation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent isolation or extinguishant discharge — an uncommanded/erroneous isolation (propulsion-unit contactor open, feather, or fuel shutoff) or extinguishant bottle discharge with no actual fire/thermal event.
fha.effAc: Inadvertent nacelle isolation opens a propulsion-unit contactor and feathers a propeller, removing one propulsion unit; inadvertent fuel shutoff removes the turbogenerator source; inadvertent generator-bay extinguishant discharge expends the single bottle (no reserve). Each removes a propulsion or energy path or the sole suppression means with no fire present.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise a false isolation/discharge, manage the resulting asymmetry or loss of a source, and are left with no extinguishant reserve for a subsequent generator-bay fire; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Reduced propulsion/energy margin during the affected phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent isolation removes one of two propulsion/energy paths (the sizing case is continuation on one unit) and inadvertent discharge expends the sole generator-bay bottle — a significant reduction in functional capability and increase in crew workload; classified Major pending confirmation of the worst single inadvertent action and phase. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous containment vent indication — the store containment vent state reported to the displays is incorrect (indicates vented/contained when it is not, or vice versa).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Condition id SF-012-M2 is not present in the current FCIM for SF-012 (the matrix carries TL/PL/M and Unaware M3 only), and the SDD states the vent state is reported as displayed data but does not define a crew action driven by that indication, so no aircraft effect can be grounded; needs the intended crew use of the vent indication and the true-vs-indicated cases before a severity can be derived. Emitted per turn instruction; not model-backed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of containment or suppression — the containment (store-bay enclosure/overboard vent) or the suppression means (generator-bay bottle, nacelle isolation) is unavailable and the crew are not aware of it.
fha.effAc: Should a fire or thermal-runaway event occur, the designed response is absent without warning: a store-bay module event may not be contained/vented overboard, or a generator-bay fire may not be extinguished, or a nacelle event may not be isolated — the protection is silently defeated. No effect until an event occurs, then the aircraft is exposed to an uncontained/unsuppressed fire or thermal event.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally believing protection is available; on an event they act on a suppression/containment response that does not function, with no prior indication.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to an uncontained/unsuppressed fire or thermal event if one occurs.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent, undetected loss of containment or suppression removes the designed protective response for a fire/thermal event on a high-voltage-store aircraft; the crew-unaware case is a large reduction in safety margins and, combined with an event, approaches loss of the aircraft — classified Hazardous pending confirmation of which protection is lost and its criticality per zone (store-bay containment loss may warrant Catastrophic). [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire containment and suppression
fha.effAc: Detection remains but a designed response is degraded — e.g. loss of the single generator-bay extinguishant bottle, or a nacelle isolation (contactor-open/feather) path or store containment/vent partially unavailable. A fire or thermal event in the affected zone is met by a reduced set of responses; the crew retains other means (isolation, feather, procedure) but with reduced margin against an escalating fire.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to work the remaining isolation/feather procedure and manage a degraded protection state; annunciated.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect absent an actual fire; increased exposure if a fire occurs in the affected zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the aircraft depends on WHICH suppression/containment element is lost and WHETHER an actual fire is present concurrently — the FHA row alone cannot state a single worst-case aircraft outcome without that scoping (the SDD notes suppression is not redundant and containment/isolation are the primary responses). Classification requires the engineer to bound the specific degraded element and its co-incident fire assumption; abstaining rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire containment and suppression
fha.effAc: No means to contain, isolate or suppress a fire or thermal-runaway event in any designated fire zone (store bay, generator compartment, both nacelles). An in-flight fire in a high-energy zone — high-voltage energy store, turbogenerator/fuel, or a nacelle inverter — could propagate uncontained, threatening adjacent structure, the powertrain and the hull. On this hybrid amphibian the store bay and generator bay are high-energy fire zones whose containment/isolation are the designed barrier.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest an escalating fire by any designed system means; forced to an emergency descent/landing or ditching.
fha.effPax: Potential fatal injury to occupants if an uncontained fire propagates to the cabin or causes loss of the aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all fire containment/isolation/suppression, taken with a concurrent fire in a high-energy zone, admits uncontained fire propagation potentially resulting in loss of the airplane and multiple fatalities. Classified from those stated effects. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin pressure control
fha.effAc: Cabin pressure controlled to an incorrect schedule via the single outflow valve — cabin altitude driven high (toward the max operating altitude of FL120) or an incorrect differential applied. An independent positive-pressure relief valve limits over-pressure. Erroneous high cabin altitude reduces occupant oxygenation; the aircraft operates at low flight levels (cruise 8,000 ft) which bounds the achievable cabin altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous control, override the outflow valve manually, and if needed descend; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Physical discomfort to distress from an erroneous cabin altitude; bounded by the FL120 ceiling.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Worst-case occupant effect depends on the cabin altitude the erroneous control can command against the FL120/8,000 ft operating envelope and on the relief-valve limit — the SDD gives the architecture (single outflow valve, independent relief valve) but no pressure/altitude schedule, so the physiological severity cannot be derived here without that envelope data. Abstaining rather than assuming a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded cabin depressurisation
fha.effAc: Cabin loses pressurisation without command (e.g. outflow valve driven open). The aircraft is designed to fly unpressurised as a normal operating condition at/below FL120, so cabin altitude follows aircraft altitude; at typical cruise (8,000 ft) the exposure is limited. Rate of depressurisation and peak cabin altitude are not stated.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise the depressurisation (annunciated pressure sensing) and descend/adjust the outflow override as needed; workload increase.
fha.effPax: Discomfort to physical distress on rapid loss of cabin pressure; bounded by the aircraft's low operating altitudes and the by-design unpressurised operating condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This failure condition is not present in the SF-013 FCIM (the model lists only SF-013-M and SF-013-M3 for this function) — I cannot confirm it is a modelled condition to classify against. Even taken on its stated effects, severity depends on decompression rate and peak cabin altitude versus the FL120/8,000 ft envelope, which the SDD does not provide. Two grounds to abstain; the engineer should first confirm whether this row should exist in the model.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of cabin pressurisation
fha.effAc: Cabin pressurisation is lost and the crew are NOT alerted; assuming normal duties they take no action and cabin altitude rises with the loss undetected. Cabin altitude and differential sensing exist and feed the displays, so an undetected case requires that sensing/alerting also be unavailable. Bounded by the FL120 ceiling and 8,000 ft typical cruise, which limits the maximum cabin altitude the occupants can be exposed to.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; progressive hypoxia risk if cabin altitude rises to a physiologically significant level before other cues appear.
fha.effPax: Progressive hypoxia risk from undetected exposure to cabin altitude; bounded by the aircraft's low operating altitude envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The occupant severity of an UNDETECTED depressurisation turns on the maximum cabin altitude reachable within the FL120/8,000 ft envelope and the time-to-incapacitation at that altitude — physiological data and the pressure schedule the SDD does not provide. The SDD confirms pressure sensing feeds the displays but gives no alerting-loss or altitude data to bound the unaware case. Abstaining rather than assuming.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of cabin pressurisation — reduced pressurisation with cabin altitude rising above scheduled but within the operating altitude envelope
fha.effAc: Cabin differential reduces; cabin altitude climbs above schedule but remains bounded by the FL120 maximum operating altitude. No effect on aircraft controllability, structure or propulsion.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by cabin differential/altitude indication (state to displays per §5.16.4); crew descends toward a habitable cabin altitude per procedure. Slight increase in workload to monitor and manage descent.
fha.effPax: Mild physiological discomfort (ear/sinus) during the altitude change; no incapacitation within the operating altitude envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor MIN-3 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin pressurisation — cabin unable to maintain any differential; cabin altitude equals aircraft altitude
fha.effAc: Cabin differential lost; cabin altitude equals aircraft altitude, bounded by the FL120 maximum operating altitude. No effect on aircraft controllability, structure or propulsion; the SDD notes unpressurised flight on stored energy is an operating condition consistent with FL120.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted (pack/valve and differential state to displays); crew descends to a habitable cabin altitude per procedure. Increase in workload to manage the descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Physical discomfort/distress during exposure to cabin altitude up to the FL120 ceiling until descent; effect bounded by the operating altitude limit rather than a high-altitude rapid-decompression case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor MAJ-3 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin temperature control — cabin temperature driven away from selected setpoint (over-heating or over-cooling)
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability, structure or propulsion.
fha.effCrew: Crew notices temperature deviation; selects manual temperature adjustment or reverts to the recirculation/heater path. Slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Thermal discomfort to passengers until corrected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor MIN-3 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded loss of cabin ventilation — ventilation airflow to the flight deck and cabin ceases without command, crew aware
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability, structure or propulsion.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted (pack/valve state to displays); reverts to the electrical recirculation-fan path on channel 2 or descends. Increase in workload to reconfigure.
fha.effPax: Progressive cabin air quality/thermal discomfort until the recirculation path is restored or descent completed; no incapacitation within the operating altitude envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: — [anchor MIN-3 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of cabin ventilation — ventilation airflow ceases with no annunciation, crew unaware and continuing duties normally
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability, structure or propulsion.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no action regarding the condition (unaware); cabin air quality degrades unnoticed until physiological cues appear, at which point workload rises to diagnose and reconfigure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the passenger effect of a fully UNDETECTED ventilation loss depends on cabin air-exchange rate, occupant CO2/temperature accumulation over exposure time, and whether any independent physiological cue reaches the crew — none of which are stated in the SDD. Needs the ventilation-loss habitability time-to-effect data before a severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of cabin ventilation and temperature control
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability or structural function; cabin airflow/temperature degraded from intended.
fha.effCrew: Reduced thermal comfort; possible slight increase in crew workload to manage cabin conditions manually via temperature select and outflow override.
fha.effPax: Physical discomfort to passengers (reduced ventilation/temperature control) within a habitable envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are physical discomfort to passengers and a slight increase in crew workload with no reduction in safety margins. [anchor MIN-3 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin ventilation and temperature control
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability or structural function; cabin ventilation and temperature control unavailable.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload managing a degraded cabin environment; potential distraction over a prolonged coastal sector (up to ~70 min cruise).
fha.effPax: Physical distress to passengers from loss of ventilation and temperature control over the sector duration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity between Minor and Major turns on the cabin temperature/CO2/ventilation envelope reached with total ECS ventilation loss over sector duration, and whether crew workload/passenger distress crosses the discomfort threshold; the SDD states the function but not the achievable degraded-cabin conditions or exposure limits, so the aircraft effect cannot be pinned to a class without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of windscreen anti-fog
fha.effAc: No effect on controllability; partial windscreen fogging reduces forward external visibility.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload to manage degraded forward visibility; reliance on remaining clear areas and instruments.
fha.effPax: No effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial anti-fog loss produces a slight reduction in forward visibility and a slight increase in crew workload with instrument reference retained; no reduction in safety margins is supported by the stated effects. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of windscreen anti-fog
fha.effAc: No effect on controllability; complete windscreen fogging obscures forward external visibility during visual segments of approach and landing.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to maintain external references for a water or paved landing; degraded ability to acquire the surface visually.
fha.effPax: No effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Total loss of forward external visibility during a water/paved approach and landing could reduce safety margins, but the SDD does not state the degree of obscuration achievable, whether side-window or instrument references suffice, or the visual-reference requirement for the coastal approach; without that the aircraft effect cannot be committed to Minor vs Major.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded right thrust change
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in right thrust produces a thrust asymmetry the crew must counter with yaw/roll input; magnitude and phase determine whether a safety-margin reduction results, most demanding at low-speed high-thrust phases (take-off, go-around).
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the yaw/asymmetry cue and thrust indication and counter with rudder/aileron and thrust-lever adjustment to restore symmetric thrust.
fha.effPax: Possible transient lateral acceleration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded asymmetric thrust excursion at low speed imposes a large reduction in safety margins / functional capability while the crew arrest and correct it; classified HAZ-1 on that effect. Confirm against the aircraft-level controllability/asymmetry analysis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous right thrust command
fha.effAc: An erroneous right thrust command that the crew do not detect produces a sustained thrust asymmetry or incorrect thrust setting with no corrective action taken, degrading trajectory control and, in the take-off/climb phases, climb performance and directional margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding the erroneous command (unaware case); the misleading thrust state persists uncorrected.
fha.effPax: Sustained off-nominal flight path.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects direction is clear (uncorrected erroneous asymmetric thrust degrades directional and climb margins), but whether an undetected erroneous single-unit thrust command reaches a large reduction in safety margins (HAZ-1) versus loss of control depends on the credible authority/rate of the erroneous command and the aircraft-level controllability response — not stated at aircraft-function level. Needs the asymmetry/controllability analysis to fix the class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of right propulsion thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced thrust available from the right unit; symmetric-thrust capability degraded and total installed thrust reduced, giving a reduction in climb/acceleration margins, most demanding on take-off and go-around.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe reduced thrust/powertrain indication and manage thrust asymmetry, adjusting the operating point within remaining rating.
fha.effPax: Possible reduced climb rate.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial thrust loss on one unit leaves the pair still producing thrust and the aircraft controllable, but with a significant reduction in performance/safety margins requiring crew management; classified MAJ-1 on that effect. Confirm against the performance case. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of right propulsion thrust
fha.effAc: Total loss of right-unit thrust leaves the aircraft on the left unit alone with the failed propeller requiring feather for the remaining unit's rating to suffice; large reduction in climb/performance margins and a thrust asymmetry to be trimmed, most critical in take-off/climb.
fha.effCrew: Crew identify the failed unit, feather its propeller and continue the sector on the remaining unit, managing asymmetry and reduced performance; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Reduced climb performance; continued flight to a suitable base.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one of two propulsion units is a large reduction in functional capability and safety margins with the sizing case being continuation of the sector on the remaining unit after feathering the failed side; classified HAZ-1. Not Catastrophic because the pair is sized for single-unit continuation. Confirm against the OEI performance/controllability case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent propeller feather
fha.effAc: Inadvertent feather of one propeller removes that unit's thrust, producing a sudden thrust asymmetry and loss of that unit's contribution equivalent in effect to a single-unit thrust loss; most critical at low-speed high-thrust phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the yaw/thrust cue, counter the asymmetry and continue on the remaining unit, managing reduced performance; feather is a guarded overhead switch and also auto-commanded on locked rotor.
fha.effPax: Reduced climb performance; lateral transient.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent feather removes one of two units' thrust and imposes a thrust asymmetry — a large reduction in safety margins/functional capability the crew must arrest, equivalent in aircraft effect to single-unit thrust loss; classified HAZ-1. Confirm against the same OEI/asymmetry case as SF-005-TL. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The applicable certification basis is 14 CFR Part 23 normal category, Level 4/high-speed, AC 23.1309-1E Class III, as declared in the SDD — not the Part 25 basis recorded in the project state.
assumptions.rationale: CURRENT PROJECT STATE carries certBasis Part 25, but the source SDD §1.3 declares an intended Part 23 Class III basis; the decomposition itself is basis-agnostic but every downstream severity objective depends on which governs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If Part 25 governs, downstream AFHA severity-to-probability objectives use the Part 25 ladder (Catastrophic 1e-9/fh etc.) rather than AC 23.1309-1E Class III; the function set above is unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: All add_function rows (framing for downstream AFHA), no severity authored.

citations.quote: The intended certification basis is 14 CFR Part 23, normal category, at Level 4 / high-speed

assumptions.text: HUF and HUA structural/watertight integrity is a structural-analysis and Particular-Risk item, not an aircraft function, so only the hull's water directional-control BEHAVIOUR is authored as a function.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 tags HUF/HUA as 'Structural'; the modeling rule excludes structural integrity from the functional FHA, and the SDD itself (§5.12.3) says hull behaviour 'is structure ... set at build'.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants hull watertight integrity captured as a function, an additional 'maintain hull watertight integrity' function and its compartment sub-functions would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Omission of a hull-integrity function; retention of 'Provide directional control on the water'.

assumptions.text: Electrical distribution (EL1/EL2), the energy store (EST), the turbogenerator (EGN) and thermal management (TMS) are resources and are NOT authored as aircraft functions.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 explicitly classifies these five as resources that supply other systems; the modeling rule forbids authoring resources as functions or failure conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must appear as a function, additional add_function rows would be required and the golden-thread would trace consumer functions to a function rather than to the Resources model.
assumptions.usedFor: Deliberate omission of PRL-bus/EST/EGN/TMS/EL1/EL2 as functions.

assumptions.text: The five systems the SDD labels resources (EST, EGN, TMS, EL1, EL2) are excluded from the aircraft-function set and will be captured in the Resources model rather than as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly designates these as resources, and the house rule bars authoring power/energy/thermal supply as functions; no function rows were created for them.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be treated as a function (e.g. an aircraft-level 'provide propulsion energy' function is required by the AFHA), an additional top-level function and its sub-functions would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of EST/EGN/TMS/EL1/EL2 from the function list.
